extracted.intended_audience: early-career mathematicians, graduate students, postdocs, and researchers planning careers in mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Career-advice guidance for mathematicians on how to set goals, choose problems, and make institutional and grant decisions while remaining adaptable to changing circumstances in research. Emphasizes realistic planning, multiple directions, and learning outside one's initial specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term goals 'should not be set in stone, and should be updated when new developments occur.' Research is unpredictable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat long-term aims as provisional; regularly revise goals in light of new results, techniques, collaborations, or shifts in interest. Avoid rigid long-term commitments that don't account for unpredictable progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not announce work on famous problems before having a feasible plan; doing so can make it 'harder to gracefully abandon the problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publicly tying your identity or programme to solving a famous problem unless you have a realistic strategy and some intermediate progress. Premature public commitment can create reputational and practical obstacles to changing direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant proposal realism (don't promise to 'solve X' without plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stating 'I will solve <Famous Problem X>' in grant proposals lacks credibility without a coherent plan and demonstrated progress on intermediate milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals, prefer staged, realistic objectives and clearly articulated intermediate milestones rather than grand unqualified claims. Funders expect credible methods and evidence of feasibility, not unsupported promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make career decisions based on institutional fit, not single faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't choose institutions based on single faculty members; they may relocate or your interests may shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate departments and institutions for broader resources, culture, and stability rather than relying solely on one collaborator or hire. Anticipate that personnel and personal interests change, so prefer robust institutional environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive adaptation to emerging developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Be responsive and adapt to emerging developments in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor new results and trends and be prepared to pivot or incorporate them into your work. Responsiveness helps keep your research relevant and opens new productive directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to explore new problems and fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Be willing to explore new problems and fields that prove more interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not feel constrained to your initial specialty; moving into adjacent or new fields can lead to better match with your interests and more impactful work. Treat exploration as a positive research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn tools and knowledge outside initial specialty
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively learn tools and knowledge outside one's initial specialty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire techniques, methods, and background from other areas when they help address current problems. Cross-training increases flexibility and problem-solving options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use realistic, staged approaches to challenging problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach hard problems in realistic stages with intermediate milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break large or famous problems into tractable subproblems and set achievable interim goals; this both increases credibility (e.g., for grants) and prevents wasted effort on unrealistic single-step plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain multiple research directions rather than obsessive focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain multiple research directions instead of obsessively focusing on a single goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify your research portfolio so that setbacks in one direction don't derail your career. Multiple productive projects increase stability, learning opportunities, and chances of impactful results.
